<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Register accepted speculative tokens in the local prefix cache before terminal cleanup releases their blocks. Follow-up to the GPU-cache question on [#52771](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52771#issuecomment-5507841294).

## Claims

- A finished speculative request publishes its finalized KV before cleanup, restoring reuse of accepted draft tokens by a later request.
- The registration excludes later in-flight work and verifier output trimmed by stopping, and retains the coordinator's existing MTP safety fence.
- An async Mamba retry preserves the durable copy-on-write cache entry instead of also attaching its key to mutable request state.

## Validation

Refreshed locally on 2026-10-11 against `main` at `2339bd39d661`; candidate head `0f646d824d51`.

The scheduler-hunk ablation reproduces these reuse differences on that base:

| CPU scheduler case | Without scheduler fix | With fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary K=3 speculative decode | 32 tokens | 48 tokens |
| Emulated multi-module MTP, sync | 0 tokens | 16 tokens |
| Emulated multi-module MTP, async | 0 tokens | 16 tokens |

Fresh local checks, using the shared test environment with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` and the checkout on `PYTHONPATH` (final focused/adjacent and ablation runs also used `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`):

- Focused regressions and safety cases: **8 passed**.
- Remove scheduler hunk: **3 failed, 5 passed**, precisely the three publication cases above.
- Remove Mamba guard: **1 failed, 7 passed**, precisely the copy-on-write ownership case.
- Move the async guard before checkpoint cleanup: **1 failed, 7 passed**, precisely the transient-checkpoint hash cleanup case.
- Adjacent Mamba/EAGLE, partial-prefix, async-scheduler, Mamba-align and prefix-cache suites: **428 passed**.
- Full scheduler file: **166 passed, 45 failed**. Exact-base control: **161 passed, the same 45 failed**. Failure IDs and messages match; all are multimodal/encoder tests blocked by local model inspection (`torchvision` is missing). The local environment also lacks `vllm._C`. No additional failing case was introduced.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering; `git diff --check` passed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_finished_spec_decode_registers_accepted_tokens \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py::test_finished_request_does_not_cache_in_flight_tokens \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py::test_hybrid_mamba_partial_tail_owner_uses_cow_on_continue \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py::test_transient_checkpoint_evicts_retained_boundary_hash -q

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_mamba_eagle_resume_checkpoint.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -q

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
git diff --check HEAD^..HEAD
```

</details>

Historical model validation, **not repeated for this refresh**: a 2026-09-10 A/B on one RTX A6000, `n=1` per arm, used `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` at `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, fp16, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, eager synchronous V1 execution, block size 16, APC, K=3 ngram speculation and greedy sampling. Baseline Python source `9e257065601` reused 32 tokens; patched source `38be1bf93a2` reused 48, with identical output tokens/text and all three drafts accepted. Both used precompiled extensions from `08b3e67b669`. The scheduler hunk is unchanged in this refresh. That run validates the ordinary attention/ngram boundary, not throughput, current-main serving, hybrid Mamba, or real MTP; this refresh's Mamba coverage is CPU testing.

## Details

The last speculative verification may accept tokens after the normal allocation-time cache registration. If the same output terminates the request, there is no later allocation pass to register them. Before freeing a request that entered stop handling as `RUNNING` and actually finished, the existing cache coordinator now registers:

```python
min(max(0, request.num_computed_tokens - request.num_in_flight_tokens),
    request.num_tokens)
```

The new terminal call can retry a Mamba partial boundary already moved to a durable copy-on-write block. While async work remains in flight, a boundary at or behind the optimistic computed frontier must not be reattached to the mutable request-table source. First publication beyond that frontier remains allowed. The guard follows mandatory eviction of transient/unretained checkpoints and preserves #60533's revised boundary calculation and validation. The cleanup test now uses periodic retention to exercise a transient intermediate checkpoint, and retries only the settled 127-token prefix when one of 128 tokens is in flight. It adds no device synchronization, public API, or model-runner change.

Scope is local/core prefix-cache registration. This does not claim propagation of the newly published terminal Mamba state through an external KV connector.

**Duplicate and related-work check (2026-10-11):** reread #52771 and searched open and merged work for terminal cache registration, accepted tokens and references to #54979. The fresh scheduler ablation proves the missing registration remains on this exact base. #60533 changes hybrid checkpoint boundaries, not this terminal call. Merged #60071 preserves existing GPU publication while fixing SimpleCPU offload selection, and explicitly identifies #54979 as separate. #57646 exposes offload metadata; #58668 fixes resumable stop-trimmed accounting and explicitly preserves this PR's terminal cap. #53802 changes prompt-boundary reachability. #50551 predates this work and deserves credit for finalized Mamba decode checkpoints; its opt-in recurrent checkpoint mechanism does not register the ordinary attention/ngram terminal case reproduced here. #52244 also predates this work and deserves credit for its hybrid prompt-tail/replay corrections, which address a different lifecycle boundary. Concurrent Mamba changes must be composed if they land first.

AI assistance (Claude and OpenAI Codex) was used for investigation, regression tests, the refresh and drafting.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Uses the existing cache coordinator; 30 added production lines and no new interface.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Reproducer, isolated negative controls, adjacent suites and exact-base scheduler comparison; historical GPU evidence is explicitly scoped.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Problem, boundaries, evidence, related work and limitations documented.
</details>
